name: MAD_V7_REEL_BEST_PRACTICES
license_note: Curated short original guidance informed by linked first-party/official sources; do not treat any passage as policy higher than owner consent or verified footage.

items.text: Begin with the clearest visual or emotional promise drawn from recorded footage; an opening hook must not claim unseen outcomes.
For a calm wellness story, open on an expressive sensory detail such as steam, light, breathing or water, then reveal its context; avoid loud gimmicks.
Use one coherent creative idea per short vertical Reel. Remove secondary messages that disrupt the emotional through-line.
Let the first selected shot establish mood and curiosity; choose a later reveal only when that progression is supported by actual clips.
A concise cinematic arc can follow invitation, sensory immersion, gentle turning point and satisfying final visual; adapt to footage length.
Sequence verified shots to preserve a plausible continuity of movement, lighting and activity, even when the final order differs from capture order.
Never invent guests, facial expressions, reviews, activities, venues, therapeutic benefits or scenes absent from the real supplied footage.
Use a visual motif such as steam, water or natural texture to connect disparate shots without adding fabricated media.
Avoid repetitive shot order and identical hooks across episodes; favor fresh, evidence-based approaches within the owner's brief.
For vertical social video, protect faces, hands and the strongest visual subject; use a compositionally intentional 9:16 crop.
Keep important captions and logos inside the platform-safe central area, avoiding covered bottom and top interface regions.
Inspect at native resolution and on a phone-sized preview; do not assume the desktop composition remains legible on a handset.
Use wide-to-close visual contrast and deliberate subject placement as an editing choice, not a requirement to reframe every shot.
If a crop removes relevant context or cuts off a person's face, reject the treatment instead of claiming the effect was applied successfully.
Let pacing follow meaningful action and the music or natural sound rather than applying uniform cuts at fixed intervals.
Preserve enough dwell time for viewers to perceive important actions, text and emotions; shorten only redundant footage.
Use restrained rhythm changes to emphasize a turning point: longer breathing shots can contrast with a brief sequence of details.
Transitions must be intentionally motivated by shape, movement, sound or narrative; avoid decorative transitions without purpose.
Reject transitions that create black frames, stutters, unexpected speed jumps, missing audio or broken continuity.
items.source_title: MAD Reel Engine V7 Technical Baseline

items.text: Choose a consistent color temperature and contrast appropriate to the actual location, preserving natural skin and material textures.
Favor restrained highlights, balanced shadows and clear subject separation; avoid over-saturation and heavy artificial cinematic filters.
Assess adjacent shots together for flickering exposure, drastic color mismatch, crushed shadows and clipped highlights.
Keep on-screen language short, high-contrast and readable in a phone-safe central area; time phrases to complete on a natural edit beat.
Prefer a unified caption treatment over competing title styles; typography should support the image rather than cover the action.
For prerecorded speech, captions need correct words, intelligible timing and relevant non-speech audio information when necessary.
Check contrast of overlaid text against moving imagery and adjust background treatment for readability where necessary.
Match authentic music mood to pacing and subject. Music must be a verifiable human-created recording with approved composition and master rights.
Preserve audible natural ambience when it strengthens presence and authenticity; do not mask important breathing, voices or environment.
Balance dialogue, natural sound and licensed music so intelligibility is not sacrificed to a louder soundtrack.
Check for abrupt starts or cutoffs, overly loud peaks, distorted fades and music finishing before the picture.
FFmpeg loudnorm can normalize an audible track, but near-silent audio needs measurement and may require preserving silence to avoid invalid encoder samples.
Never invent synthesized filler audio or claim discovered catalog metadata alone establishes the right to mix a recording.
Probe final output video and audio independently for H.264/AAC, frame size, frame rate, duration alignment and decoded integrity.
Verify the opening image, transition frames, title legibility, audience-safe framing, and final frame after actual FFmpeg output.
Treat render completed, technical QA passed, creative approved, scheduled and publicly published as distinct acceptance states.
Never mark an effect as genuinely applied merely because a prompt requested it; verify the rendered frames and output receipt.
items.source_title: MAD Reel Engine V7 Technical Baseline

items.text: Respect subject consent and footage provenance; private guest media must not be sent to unsupported external tools or published automatically.
YouTube recognizes qualifying square or vertical videos of up to three minutes as Shorts, subject to its current channel/date rules; validate requirements before publishing.
Plan a native 9:16 portrait master for Reels and Stories, with key text away from Instagram's top and bottom interface overlays.
A 30-second target is an editorial brief, not permission to extend short source footage with invented scenes or unrelated repetitive loops.
Write on-screen hooks and titles for watching with or without sound. Retain audible soundtrack for sound-on users where rights and source allow.
Use restrained grain, vignette and fades only where supported by the footage; evaluate whether a treatment improves clarity.
items.source_title: MAD Reel Engine V7 Technical Baseline

items.text: Ensure final titles resolve before the end and that audio decays naturally rather than truncating the experience mid-phrase.

Search music metadata through V5's existing Openverse audio API, restricting discovery to CC0, PDM and CC BY; obtain candidates but do not download or mix a catalog result merely because its metadata says free.
Search with a concrete sonic intention first, then retry broad terms such as ambient, piano or forest if a narrow multiword query gives no results; cap result counts and API calls.

If Openverse yields no relevant candidate or is unavailable, use the existing Wikimedia Commons MediaWiki filetype:audio discovery fallback. Examine the file's original page, author and LicenseShortName; exclude CC BY-SA, NC and ND from this V7 automatic music admission path.

An audio search result is only a suggestion. Verify the recording's original source page, its composition and master recording reuse rights, allowed license, creator credit, any platform constraints and evidence of approval before treating it as usable audio.

AI may propose one discovered external soundtrack by exact allowlisted source ID, but recommendation status is REVIEW_REQUIRED. It cannot grant rights, download unverified audio, fake a review receipt or bypass V6's independent evidence gate.

For a final reel, choose an exact SHA256 from the owner-private, independently cleared V6 recording catalog. If that catalog is empty, retain source ambience and include a shortlist for rights review; never auto-promote discovery metadata to a cleared track.

Select tempo and sonic texture to fit the actual filmed story: meditative steam, breath and water work with sparse ambient sounds; an energetic movement sequence may justify more rhythm. Avoid dialogue masking or dramatic cues unsupported by footage.

Before FFmpeg use, independently recheck approved audio bytes against SHA256, sufficient duration, readable codec and the original V6 rights evidence; mix the complete licensed recording with bounded gain, natural fades and full-length audio verification.

Do not treat Instagram's in-app song selection or Openverse indexing as a transferable license to bake that track into a separately rendered commercial Reel. The publication rights for both composition and recording remain separate checks.

Meta's Instagram professional dashboard Best Practices includes creation advice on capturing attention and Reel length, with personalized guidance. Consider the first moments of a genuine film; do not promise an algorithmic boost from a specific hook length.

Use a portrait 9:16 master and check preview-safe composition on a phone. Meta's Instagram API recommends 9:16; do not put titles or faces beneath interface overlays; evaluate each Reel's actual viewing surface.

Meta's Reels publishing API accepts MP4 or MOV with H.264/HEVC video and AAC audio, and documents 23 to 60 fps. The V7 1080x1920 H.264/AAC 30fps output is a compatible target but must be independently probed.

Check the actual destination's current limits before publishing: the official Meta Instagram API document specifies at least 3 seconds, up to 15 minutes, a 1 GB file maximum and 25 Mbps maximum video bitrate for this publishing route; these are API limits, not creative recommendations.

Instagram supports assembling multiple clips, timing changes and transitions. Plan source-grounded scenes, visual continuity and sound-aligned movement; do not add non-existent scenes or unrelated beat-sync cutaways.
Instagram's editing updates include revised fonts and text outlines for clarity. Make on-screen captions concise and readable on a mobile screen, especially when viewers have muted audio.

Instagram has described Replays and its moment-by-moment Retention Chart as Reel performance signals. After a separately approved post, evaluate actual watch retention and replay behavior rather than treating creative heuristics as guaranteed reach.

Meta Blueprint includes a dedicated lesson on Reels creative best practices and reaching existing and new audiences. Use it as a platform education reference, not authority to override authentic footage and owner editorial intent.

Trial Reels can test content with non-followers, but creating a trial is still an Instagram publishing operation. Never trigger a trial, public Reel, feed post or cross-post from RAG advice without explicit owner approval.

Instagram's original-audio and in-app music tools are editing features, not proof that a third-party commercial soundtrack is usable outside the app. Use the V5/V6 separately verified audio and keep attribution in the reel manifest.
